items.title: Housing decrees face November 12 survival vote
items.body: Two housing decrees in force since October 7 face a parliamentary vote on November 12. PNV support gives the broader package, including an eviction ban for vulnerable people until 2030 and rental extensions until 2028, a likely 35–34 majority. The separate decree requiring landlords to compensate tenants lacks a majority.

items.title: November 11 general strike: pay and rights
items.body: Unions have called a general strike for November 11 over wages, housing costs, and stalled employer talks. Workers can strike without retaliation, including when working remotely. Pay deductions cover the strike day plus proportional rest-day and extra payments; holidays are unaffected.

items.title: December sick leave gets new calculation basis
items.body: Royal Decree-law 31/2026 of October 20 applies to sick leave starting December 1. For common illness or non-work accidents, pay will use the contribution base from two months before the leave, not the previous month. Rates stay unchanged: nothing for days 1–3, 60% for days 4–20, and 75% from day 21.

items.title: PP proposes wider mortgage guarantees and VAT cuts
items.body: The PP's election programme would extend public mortgage guarantees from age 35 to under 40, potentially up to 50. It would cut first-home VAT from 10% to 4% for under-40s. The party also pledges to repeal rental limits and eviction suspensions if it wins the November 29 election.

items.title: Rail disruption cuts revenue and Andalucía services
items.body: High-speed operators lost €100.67 million in ticket revenue in the first half of 2026 as accidents, speed limits, and cancellations disrupted travel. The government said on November 3 it would cut frequencies to Andalucía after reopening the line, until a safety audit and a signalling upgrade planned for early 2027.

items.title: Rooms and seasonal lets dominate rental adverts
items.body: A Consumer Affairs ministry and CSIC study found rooms and seasonal lets made up 55.8% of rental adverts in 53 Spanish capitals before October's housing decree. Researchers say seasonal lets helped owners avoid standard tenant protections. The decree tightens these rules and is in force, but a vote to validate it is due November 12.

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz claims first Paris Masters title
items.body: World number three tennis player Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton 7-6(5), 7-5 on November 8 to win his first Paris Masters title. He saved six break points in the final. It is his fifth trophy this season and Spain's first Paris title since 2012.

items.title: Energy upgrades still qualify for tax relief
items.body: In-force IRPF (personal income tax) relief offers 20%, 40%, or up to 60% deductions for qualifying energy upgrades. Main-home deductions go up to €3,000 a year. To claim for 2026, register the post-work energy certificate before December 31; a pre-work certificate and non-cash payments are also required.

items.title: Mortgage rates rise as banks tighten lending
items.body: Spain's average mortgage rate reached 2.99% in September as banks raised prices and became more selective. Rural savings banks gained market share while CaixaBank, Sabadell, and Bankinter lost ground. Competition regulator CNMC is investigating whether six major banks' disclosures of future commercial plans breached competition rules.

items.title: Sánchez pledges yearly minimum wage rises and pension protection
items.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez pledged yearly rises in the SMI (minimum wage) and constitutional protection for pension increases at a November 8 pre-campaign rally in Bilbao. He also promised constitutional protection for abortion rights. These are campaign pledges ahead of the November 29 election, not enacted measures.

items.title: Private health cover grows as waiting concerns mount
items.body: Spain's health survey found 24% of Spaniards now hold private health insurance, 36.4% more than in 2023. A separate Barómetro Sanitario shows 72.7% think specialist waits have worsened and 67.6% say the same of diagnostic tests. Paying for alternatives remains out of reach for some households.

items.title: Overcrowded housing rises 73% over a decade
items.body: A CGT report says 9.5% of people in Spain live in overcrowded homes, up 73% over a decade. It links the rise to higher housing prices and living costs. Young people and people in poverty are especially affected; Catalunya's overcrowding rate reaches 13.1%.
